function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

Here’s a quick snapshot of some of the most anticipated **upcoming music‑and‑culture festivals happening soon across the U.S.** – all scheduled for late March through early May (typical annual windows).  

| # | Festival | Dates (next edition) | Location | Highlights |
|---|----------|----------------------|-----------|------------|
| 1 | **South By Southwest (SXSW)** | Mar 11–Mar 20, 2026 | Austin, TX | Live concerts, film premieres, interactive tech showcases. |
| 2 | **New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival** | Apr 7–Apr 12, 2026 | New Orleans, LA | World‑class jazz, blues, funk, Cajun/French‑Creole cuisine. |
| 3 | **Coachella Valley Music & Arts Festival** | Apr 14–Apr 17, 2026 | Indio, CA | Multi‑genre lineup, art installations, celebrity sightings. |
| 4 | **Lollapalooza Chicago** | May 9–May 15, 2026 | Chicago, IL | Indie rock, hip‑hop, electronic acts plus food trucks. |
| 5 | **Bonnaroo Music & Arts Festival** | Jun 8–Jun 12, 2026 | Manchester, TN | Eclectic lineups, craft beer gardens, yoga sessions. |

> *Note:* These dates reflect the usual yearly schedule. For precise ticket availability, check each festival’s official website as release dates vary year‑to‑year.

---

### How to Pick One That Fits You

| Preference | Suggested Festivals |
|------------|---------------------|
| **Rock / Alternative** | Bonnaroo, Lollapalooza |
| **Electronic / Dance** | Electric Daisy Carnival (Las Vegas, mid‑Feb), Ultra Music Festival (Miami, Feb) |
| **Jazz / Blues** | New Orleans Jazz & Heritage, Montreux Jazz (though Swiss—just for reference!) |
| **Family Friendly** | Summerfest (Milwaukee, July) – great for kids and adults alike |
| **Foodie + Culture** | Food & Wine Classic (San Francisco, Oct) – though outside your timeframe, worth noting! |

If you’re looking for something more niche—say indie folk, metalcore, or world‑music—you’ll find smaller regional festivals sprinkled throughout the country. Let me know if you’d like recommendations tailored to a particular state, musical taste, or budget range!

Feel free to ping me again once you’ve narrowed down your interests—I’m happy to dig deeper into line‑ups, travel logistics, accommodation options, or even help snag tickets when sales open.
